olivia_infra: Heads-up — we're seeing intermittent packet loss (~1-5% bursts) between pods on gpu-pool in eu-west-1a starting ~03:10 UTC. Flows are east-west and use Geneve overlay. Symptoms: short 100-500ms spikes, retransmits on app layer, correlates with pod churn from autoscaler.
ajay_sre: Can you paste the pod/node names and a quick tcpdump of one of the affected nodes? Also what MTU are we using on the tunnel interfaces?
olivia_infra: Node: euw-gpu-23, pod: gpu-trainer-7f9c. Tunnel mtu is 1450 (we reduced it historically). Quick tcpdump attached (summarized):
```
# tcpdump -nn -i geneve0 host 10.10.32.45
15:03:21.123456 IP 10.10.32.45.50022 > 10.10.40.12.50022: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12456, ack 9876, win 64240, length 111
15:03:21.123601 IP 10.10.32.45.50022 > 10.10.40.12.50022: Flags [.], ack 9876, win 64240, length 0 (RETRANSMIT)
...
```
maria_ops: Seeing the same on euw-gpu-21. dmesg on a node shows a bunch of "net: geneve: tx queue full" lines and sometimes "NETDEV_TX_ERR" on the physical NIC.
ajay_sre: tx queue full + NETDEV_TX_ERR usually points to offload/driver interactions under load. Which NIC driver/version? ethtool -i output?
olivia_infra: ethtool -i eno3: driver i40e, version 2.4.2-k. Kernel 5.15.0-rc. I also ran `ethtool -k geneve0` and saw GSO, TSO, GRO on.

ajay_sre: Try disabling GSO on the tunnel iface as a quick repro/workaround: `ip link set dev geneve0 down && ethtool -K geneve0 gso off gro off tso off && ip link set dev geneve0 up` — see if drops stop.
taylor_net: Also check for large skb fragmentation due to MTU mismatch + GSO. We used 1450 MTU but apps send large segments that get segmented in kernel -> geneve encaps can push packets over PMTU and driver may drop if offloads try to coalesce.
olivia_infra: Ran the disable-gso command on euw-gpu-23 around 03:26 UTC, immediately saw retransmits drop to near 0 during the next 10m window. App errors cleared. Putting this as temporary mitigation.
ci-bot: [deploy-bot] Noted: rollback/mitigation applied to node euw-gpu-23 by olivia_infra at 1932104786.
maria_ops: We also observed drops spike during autoscaler-driven pod creation (~10-20 pods starting simultaneously). Could be bursty ARP/neighbor updates or conntrack pressure.
ajay_sre: Check FDB and ARP rates: `bridge fdb show br0` and `ip -s neigh show dev geneve0` and kernel conntrack counters. Also capture `ss -s` on the busy node.
taylor_net: Preliminary hypothesis: combination of i40e driver regression with GSO+Geneve + bursty pod churn causing large skb requeueing -> tx queue exhaustion -> NETDEV_TX_ERR. Long-term: kernel/driver upgrade or firmware, or keep GSO off on tunnel interfaces and tune tx queue lengths and netdev watchdog.
olivia_infra: Scheduling kernel/driver upgrade window for eu-west next week. For now we'll add a daemonset to disable GSO on geneve interfaces cluster-wide as a mitigant and reduce burst size on autoscaler for gpu-pool. I'll post PR for the daemonset.
ajay_sre: Add a short runbook: if you see NETDEV_TX_ERR + geneve + retransmits -> disable GSO on tunnel, check NIC driver version, check kernel messages, scale autoscaler ramp slower.
maria_ops: Thanks — will own the runbook and the autoscaler change. Will report back after the upgrade window.
